title: Bolesławiec pottery
summary: Bolesławiec in south-west Poland is known for cream stoneware decorated with small sponge stamps in cobalt blue, green and ochre. Here you throw a jug with a handle, then press its bands with rosettes and the ringed dots known as peacock eyes.
howToPlay: Look at the small jug in the frame: that is the shape to make.
Drag across the spinning clay, row by row, to set the width of the jug; the lit outline shows the target.
Pick a colour from the swatches and tap a band to stamp it the way the target is stamped.
Press Check to see your stars.
rules: The jug has twelve rows; each row can be set from narrow to wide.
Shape counts for most of the score, the stamped bands for the rest.
Each band must carry the colour shown on the target; the stamp (rosette, peacock eye, dots) follows the band.
Undo takes back your last change; Reshape returns to the clay.
Three stars for a close shape with every band in the right colour.
heritageNote: Potters in and around Bolesławiec in Lower Silesia have worked the local clay for centuries, and the town became famous for hard stoneware in the seventeenth century. The cream body is decorated with patterns pressed on with small cut sponges, then covered with a clear glaze and fired hot.
